blockers.title: Edge-accessibility frame cannot be installed without changing openBranch_countermodel/tableau_complete's byte-stable signatures, or IForces's definition
blockers.detail: IForces (Kripke.lean:81) is generic over [Preorder World]; its .imp case resolves '<=' via typeclass search on World. openBranch_countermodel and tableau_complete both state IForces (intExtractValuation b) (S.modelBot b) 0 phi with intExtractValuation b : Nat -> Atom -> Prop (Soundness.lean:1811, unchanged type) and 0 : Nat, so World unifies to Nat and Lean resolves [Preorder Nat] to the unique global Nat.instPreorder -- confirmed live via '#synth Preorder Nat' (concurrent session). This resolution happens at theorem-type elaboration time, before any proof-body tactic (letI/haveI) could override it, so no completeness-side-only edit can install edge-accessibility for these two theorems without changing their stated types.
blockers.counterexample: Report 08's adversarial example, re-verified: branch carries T((not p) -> q)@0 on an open saturated branch. Pick phantom world k strictly larger than every branch label. intExtractValuation b j p = False for every phantom j, so IForces k (not p) is vacuously True (antecedent always False), but IForces k q = False (phantom). This refutes 'forall w'>=0, w' forces (not p) -> w' forces q' -- the T(->) truth-lemma case (sorry 409) is genuinely FALSE at World=Nat/canonical order, for any branch containing this shape of T-implication.
blockers.new_finding_beyond_report_08: Nat.instPreorder is a LINEAR (total) order; general intuitionistic Kripke-completeness requires NON-LINEAR (tree/DAG-shaped) frames (e.g. two beta-split sibling worlds are edge-incomparable, yet both receive SOME Nat label under a total order). No relabelling/retraction of edge-accessible worlds onto bare Nat can make a total order represent a genuinely non-linear accessibility relation -- the obstruction is type-theoretic, not merely a missing proof.
blockers.additional_finding_this_dispatch: EVEN IF the signature-pinning issue above is resolved (option a or b below), intExtractValuation monotonicity along edges is SEPARATELY entangled with the B2 fuel-sufficiency argument (Phase 6-10, not yet implemented): intApplyRuleFull (Rules.lean:245-268) maps every .pos,.imp signed formula (every T(phi->psi)) to .notApplicable, so T(->) is handled exclusively by the fuel-bounded applyPersistenceFixpoint, and intStepBranch b e nw = none (the only saturation witness for the returned branch) does NOT guarantee that fixpoint loop actually converged. Atom monotonicity for T(->)-triggered atoms co-inductively depends on the antecedent formula's OWN monotonicity, resolved only by repeated applyPersistenceFixpoint passes -- i.e. by fuel. This is a wave-ordering inversion: Phase 2 (Wave 2) becomes logically dependent on Phase 10's intExpMeasure/fuel-sufficiency machinery (Wave 6). Documented in-file at Scheme.lean (doc comment immediately after intAccessPreorder_le_of_isAccessible, no sorry).

Directly reusable once the signature-pinning question (option a/b) is resolved in a re-plan; is exactly the Preorder instance option (a) would install.
blockers.recommendation: Requires a human/orchestrator-level architectural decision before Phase 2 can proceed. Two escape routes, both outside 'completeness-side edits + read-only soundness machinery': (a) change openBranch_countermodel's/tableau_complete's stated conclusion types to quantify over a new World type carrying intAccessPreorder (or similar) -- a deliberate, tracked public-signature change, requiring Postmortem Constraint 5 to be revised in a plan v6, plus an audit of all Decidable/DecisionProcedure consumers; (b) change IForces's definition (Kripke.lean) to take an explicit accessibility relation parameter instead of relying on [Preorder World] -- a foundational semantics change rippling into the already-green tableau_sound (same file, task-316-adjacent) and other IForces consumers, forbidden without escalation per Postmortem 4. EITHER WAY, the monotonicity discharge itself should be restructured as a field/hypothesis threaded alongside sat_timp (Phase 4) and discharged only once measure <= fuel (Phase 10) is available, per this dispatch's additional finding above.
